texts.li: Last night's card game went late, and by the end {B_nameDef} had bet {B_possessive} good coat on a pair of twos. {A_nameDef} has been wearing it around the colony ever since, remarking on how warm it is.\n\n{B_nameDef} says the deck was marked; {A_nameDef} says {B_nameDef} just can't count. Both want the council to rule on it.

{A_nameDef} won a week of {B_nameDef}'s dinners at dice, fair and square, in front of witnesses. Three days in, {B_nameDef} is living on scraps and spite and has started eyeing {A_nameDef}'s plate.\n\n"A bet is a bet," says {A_nameDef}. Everyone else would like the council to step in before somebody gets stabbed with a fork.

li.label: A bet is a bet. Pay up, {B_nameDef}
li.outcome: The debt stands. {A_nameDef} is enjoying the winnings loudly, and {B_nameDef} is learning a valuable lesson quietly.
li.riskOutcome: The debt stands, and {B_nameDef} decided to pay it in fists instead.

li.label: Call the bet off
li.outcome: The council voided the bet. {A_nameDef} handed back the winnings one slow finger at a time.

li.label: Ban gambling in the colony
li.outcome: The council banned gambling and voided every debt. The cards went in the fire; the dice went somewhere nobody will admit to.

li.label: Double or nothing: one more hand
li.outcome: One more hand, with the whole council watching. {A_nameDef} won again, and {B_nameDef} now owes twice as much and spends a lot of time staring at the horizon.
li.riskOutcome: One more hand, with the whole council watching. {B_nameDef} won it all back, and {A_nameDef} is now the one insisting the deck was marked.

texts.li: {B_nameDef} went into {A_nameDef}'s room looking for a borrowed hammer and found a hoard: the good knives, the softest blanket in the colony, every missing spoon, and {COUNT} {THING} nobody can account for.\n\n{A_nameDef} calls it a collection. {B_nameDef} calls it theft. The council has to call it something.

Things have been going missing for weeks: a spoon here, a shirt there, the nice chair. {B_nameDef} finally followed the scuff marks to {A_nameDef}'s room, where all of it was neatly arranged, along with {COUNT} {THING} tucked under the mattress.\n\n{A_nameDef} says it was being kept safe. From whom, {A_nameDef} won't say, and {B_nameDef} wants it all back by supper.

li.label: Confiscate the lot
li.outcome: The hoard went back into the stockpiles, {THING} and all. {A_nameDef} watched every spoon leave.
li.riskOutcome: The hoard went back into the stockpiles. {A_nameDef} did not take it well, and the furniture is paying for it.

li.label: Let {A_nameDef} keep it
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} keeps the collection. {B_nameDef} has started hiding things, which is hard, because nothing here locks.

li.label: Split it: half back to the stores
li.outcome: Half the hoard went back to the stores, including {A_nameDef}'s least favorite spoons. Nobody is happy, which apparently means it was fair.

texts.li: {A_nameDef} woke half the colony last night screaming about fire: the fields burning, the sky burning, everyone standing in the smoke without faces. It was a very detailed dream, and {A_nameDef} has described it at every meal since.\n\nPeople have started checking the horizon. The council has to decide what to do about its prophet.

Three nights running, {A_nameDef} has dreamed the same thing: smoke over the walls, a red sky, and a voice counting backward from ten. {A_nameDef} is certain it means something.\n\nA few people are starting to agree, which is worse. Somebody has to tell them whether to be afraid.

li.label: Take it seriously: double the watch
li.outcome: The council doubled the watch and told everyone to keep their eyes open. {A_nameDef} feels heard. Everyone else is sleeping badly.

li.label: Laugh it off at dinner
li.outcome: The council made a joke of it at dinner. Everyone laughed except {A_nameDef}, who has stopped telling people about dreams.
li.riskOutcome: The council made a joke of it at dinner. {A_nameDef} left halfway through, walked out past the fields, and hasn't come back yet.

li.label: Let {A_nameDef} hold a little ceremony
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} had everyone write their fears on scraps of wood and burn them on a bonfire. It felt silly. It also worked, mostly.

li.label: Tell {A_nameDef} to keep it quiet
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} has been asked to stop sharing dreams at breakfast. The dreams haven't stopped. The sharing has, mostly.

texts.li: Years ago, long before this colony, a band from {FACTION} found {A_nameDef} half-dead in a ditch and nursed {A_objective} back to health without asking for a thing. Word has come that they've had a hard season.\n\n{A_nameDef} wants to send them silver. It's the colony's silver, so it's the council's call.

{A_nameDef} never talks much about the time before. Last night, after a beer, it came out: {FACTION} took {A_nameDef} in once when nobody else would, and {A_nameDef} left without a word of thanks.\n\nNow {A_nameDef} wants to make it right, with the colony's silver, and is asking the council for it.

li.label: Send them 100 silver
li.outcome: A hundred silver went to {FACTION} with a short letter from {A_nameDef}. The reply was warm. The colony's purse is lighter.
li.riskOutcome: The silver went out with a passing caravan and never reached {FACTION}. Somewhere out there, a bandit is having a very good week.

li.label: Send a token: 25 silver
li.outcome: {FACTION} got 25 silver and a polite note. {A_nameDef} wrote the note and did not enjoy writing it.

li.label: Send them food instead
li.outcome: A load of food went to {FACTION}, who needed it more than silver anyway. The storeroom echoes a little now.

li.label: We need it more than they do
li.outcome: The council kept the silver. {A_nameDef} said nothing at all, and has been very quiet since.

texts.li: {B_nameDef} knocked a shelf while cleaning, and {A_nameDef}'s little carved bird went with it. It was the only thing {A_nameDef} still had from home. It is now four things.\n\n{B_nameDef} keeps saying it was an accident, a little too often, and {A_nameDef} wants the council to do something about it.

{A_nameDef} carried an old pocket watch that hadn't worked in years. {B_nameDef} borrowed it to fix it, as a surprise, and handed it back in a cupped palm.\n\n{A_nameDef} is grieving over a handful of springs. {B_nameDef} is very sorry and would like that to be the end of it.

li.label: {B_nameDef} apologizes in front of everyone
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} apologized at dinner, in front of everyone. It was stiff, but it was said, and {A_nameDef} nodded at the end.
li.riskOutcome: {B_nameDef} apologized at dinner through clenched teeth. Everyone heard the teeth.

li.label: The council pays {A_nameDef} 50 silver
li.outcome: The council paid {A_nameDef} fifty silver for the loss. It doesn't fix anything, and everyone knows it, but it was something.

li.label: Have {B_nameDef} make a new one
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} spent three evenings making a replacement. It isn't the same, but {A_nameDef} keeps it on the shelf where the old one was.
li.riskOutcome: {B_nameDef} spent three evenings on a replacement. It looks like the original, if the original had been described to {B_nameDef} by a drunk.

li.label: Accidents happen. Let it go
li.outcome: The council called it an accident. {A_nameDef} has kept the pieces, and an eye on {B_nameDef}.

texts.li: With raiders seen in the hills, {B_nameDef} had the night watch. {A_nameDef} came out in the small hours and found {B_nameDef} curled up against the wall, snoring. The only thing on guard was a squirrel, and it looked confused.\n\n{A_nameDef} wants it dealt with before the next dark.

{A_nameDef} came to the council at dawn, white with anger. {B_nameDef} slept through the entire watch last night, including the part where something large spent an hour sniffing at the gate.\n\nNothing got in. {A_nameDef} wants to know what the council plans to do about next time.

li.label: Punish {B_nameDef} with extra shifts
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} is hauling and digging from dawn to dusk until the council says otherwise. Nobody is sleeping on watch this week.
li.riskOutcome: {B_nameDef} took the punishment, then took a swing at {A_nameDef} for reporting it.

li.label: Warn {B_nameDef} quietly
li.outcome: The council had a quiet word with {B_nameDef}, who swore it won't happen again. {A_nameDef} has started checking on the watch personally.
li.riskOutcome: The council had a quiet word with {B_nameDef}. Two nights later {B_nameDef} was asleep on watch again, and this time everybody knows.

li.label: Put {A_nameDef} in charge of the watch
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} now runs the night watch, with a schedule, a whistle and no sense of humor about any of it. {B_nameDef} is on the schedule a lot.

li.label: Nobody died. Let it go
li.outcome: The council let it go. {A_nameDef} has stopped sleeping well, and keeps getting up to check the gate.
li.riskOutcome: The council let it go. {A_nameDef} didn't, and the argument with {B_nameDef} ended in fists.

texts.li: {A_nameDef}'s new sculpture stands right by the dining table, and it is unmistakably {B_nameDef}, down to the squint. The nose is bigger than the real one, which is saying something.\n\n{B_nameDef} has started eating outside and wants the thing gone. {A_nameDef} calls it honest art.

{A_nameDef} calls the new piece "Study of a Colonist, Mid-Excuse." Everyone else calls it {B_nameDef}, and laughs.\n\n{B_nameDef} has asked the council, very calmly, to have it removed before {B_nameDef} removes it personally, along with {A_nameDef}'s hands.

li.label: Smash it
li.outcome: The council had the sculpture smashed. {B_nameDef} swept up the pieces personally, smiling. {A_nameDef} watched from the doorway.
li.riskOutcome: The council had the sculpture smashed, and {A_nameDef} went to pieces along with it.

li.label: Keep it on display
li.outcome: The sculpture stays. Visitors love it. {B_nameDef} has taken to eating facing the wall.
li.riskOutcome: The sculpture stays. {B_nameDef} finally snapped over breakfast and went for the artist instead of the art.

li.label: Make {A_nameDef} carve an apology piece
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} carved a second {B_nameDef}, this one noble, square-jawed and gazing into the distance. {B_nameDef} pretends not to like it.
li.riskOutcome: {A_nameDef} carved an apology piece. It is technically flattering. It is also, technically, wearing a dunce cap.

texts.li: {A_nameDef} built something that is either a fiddle or a crime, and practices on it every night after everyone else has gone to bed. {B_nameDef} sleeps on the other side of the wall and has not slept, as such, in four days.\n\n{B_nameDef} came to the council red-eyed, holding a pillow like a weapon.

Every night, just as the colony settles down, the drumming starts. {A_nameDef} says it helps {A_objective} think.\n\n{B_nameDef} says it helps {B_objective} plan murders, and has asked the council, politely for now, to make it stop.

li.label: Ban the night music
li.outcome: The night music is banned. {B_nameDef} slept fourteen hours straight. {A_nameDef} has been drumming on tables, very quietly, all day.

li.label: Set quiet hours after midnight
li.outcome: Music until midnight, silence after. {A_nameDef} grumbles about artistic freedom, {B_nameDef} grumbles about the hour before midnight, and it's working.
li.riskOutcome: Quiet hours were agreed. {A_nameDef} treated them as more of a suggestion, and {B_nameDef} is back to counting ceiling cracks at three in the morning.

li.label: Tell {B_nameDef} to live with it
li.outcome: The music plays on, and {A_nameDef} is getting better, slowly. {B_nameDef} sleeps with rags stuffed in both ears and wakes up looking like a raid survivor.
li.riskOutcome: The music plays on. Two nights later {B_nameDef} snapped and started breaking things, beginning with whatever was closest.

texts.li: {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} have finally agreed on something: they want to fight. Fists only, at dawn, behind the stockpile, with the whole colony watching.\n\nThey want the council's blessing, mostly so that the loser can't complain afterward.

{B_nameDef} threw a glove at {A_nameDef}'s feet this morning. It was a work glove, used, and {A_nameDef} took that as part of the insult.\n\nThey want to settle it properly, in the yard, with witnesses. All they need is for the council to say yes.

li.label: Allow the duel
li.outcome: The duel was held at dawn, with half the colony cheering. There was blood, a loose tooth, and afterward, something like respect.

li.label: Forbid it
li.outcome: The council forbade the duel. {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} now glare at each other across every room, which is somehow worse.
li.riskOutcome: The council forbade the duel. {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} held it anyway, behind the latrine, with no witnesses and no rules.

li.label: Make them shake hands in public
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} shook hands in front of everyone. It went on for a long time and both of them had sore fingers after, but it's done.
li.riskOutcome: The handshake lasted about four seconds before it turned into a headlock.

li.label: Settle it with a hauling race instead
li.outcome: Instead of fists, {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} raced to haul a mountain of stone. The colony got a lot done, and the rivalry has turned almost friendly.
li.riskOutcome: {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} raced to haul a mountain of stone, and the loser accused the winner of cheating, at length, with fists.

texts.li: {A_nameDef} has opinions about how this colony is run, and would like them to be official. {A_nameDef} wants a formal seat on the council: a vote, a chair at the head of the table, and a title.\n\n{A_nameDef} has suggested several titles. Most of them have the word "high" in them.

{A_nameDef} pinned a list of demands to the dining room door overnight. Item one is a seat on the council. Items two through eleven assume item one.\n\nPeople are reading it over breakfast, and some of them are nodding.

li.label: Grant {A_nameDef} a title
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} is now Warden of something. Nobody is quite sure what, least of all {A_nameDef}, who has started walking differently.
li.riskOutcome: {A_nameDef} is now Warden of something, and is taking it very seriously. Several people have already been told off for sitting in the wrong chair.

li.label: Refuse the request
li.outcome: The council refused. {A_nameDef} took it calmly, the way a kettle takes heat.

li.label: Put {A_nameDef} in charge of the storeroom
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} is now in charge of the storeroom, and has labeled every shelf. Twice.
li.riskOutcome: {A_nameDef} asked for a seat at the table and was handed the storeroom keys. {A_nameDef} noticed the difference.

li.label: Let {A_nameDef} sit in on one meeting
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} sat through four hours of debate about where to dig the new latrine, and has quietly withdrawn the request.
li.riskOutcome: {A_nameDef} sat through four hours of debate about the latrine and loved every minute. {A_nameDef} now attends every meeting, uninvited, with notes.

texts.li: {A_nameDef} has been keeping a tally on the workshop wall. One column is {A_nameDef}'s hours. The other column is {B_nameDef}'s, and it's mostly empty.\n\n{A_nameDef} has started underlining things. The council is going to have to look at the wall.

{A_nameDef} came to the council with dirt up to the elbows and pointed out the window at {B_nameDef}, who was lying in the grass at noon, watching clouds. "Every day," {A_nameDef} said.\n\n{B_nameDef} says it's called thinking. {A_nameDef} says it's called lying down.

li.label: Side with {A_nameDef}: {B_nameDef} works double
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} is on double shifts until the tally evens out. {A_nameDef} updates the wall daily, with great satisfaction.
li.riskOutcome: {B_nameDef} is on double shifts, and opened the first one by throwing a shovel at {A_nameDef}.

li.label: Side with {B_nameDef}: everyone has a pace
li.outcome: The council ruled that people work at different speeds. {B_nameDef} took the ruling back out to the grass. {A_nameDef} took it badly.

li.label: Pair them up on every shift
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} now work every shift together. {B_nameDef} is picking up the pace, mostly to make the lecturing stop.
li.riskOutcome: {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} now work every shift together. {B_nameDef} has discovered that with {A_nameDef} around, {A_nameDef} does all the work.

li.label: Stay out of it
li.outcome: The council stayed out of it. The tally on the wall keeps growing, and so does the underlining.
li.riskOutcome: The council stayed out of it, so {A_nameDef} has stopped working hard on principle. If nobody's counting, why bother?

texts.li: {B_nameDef} swears that {A_nameDef} rode with the raiders who burned {B_nameDef}'s home, years ago and a long way from here. {A_nameDef} hasn't denied it. {A_nameDef} hasn't said anything at all.\n\nThe colony is quietly choosing sides, and the council needs to choose first.

It came out over dinner: an old scar, a story, the name of a place, and suddenly {B_nameDef} was on {B_possessive} feet with a knife in hand. {B_nameDef} says {A_nameDef} burned that place to the ground.\n\n{A_nameDef} says it was a long time ago, with different people, and that {A_nameDef} was someone else then. Somebody has to decide whether that's enough.

li.label: The past is past
li.outcome: The council ruled that what {A_nameDef} did before belongs to before. {B_nameDef} left the table and hasn't come back to it.
li.riskOutcome: The council ruled that the past is past. {B_nameDef} walked out of the meeting and kept walking.

li.label: {A_nameDef} works to earn a place
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} is working the hardest jobs in the colony, without complaint, until the council is satisfied. {B_nameDef} watches every shift.

li.label: Let {B_nameDef} have one swing
li.outcome: The council looked away for one minute. {B_nameDef} used all of it, and {A_nameDef} didn't raise a hand until the very end.

li.label: Bury it: nobody else needs to know
li.outcome: The council told {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} to keep it to themselves. {B_nameDef} agreed, and hasn't turned {B_possessive} back on {A_nameDef} since.
li.riskOutcome: The council tried to keep it quiet. By morning the whole colony knew, and nobody is sitting near {A_nameDef} at meals.
